source: The operator's decisions of 2026-09-26: D14, no posting more than a week old; D13, no posting he is not eligible for, and none missed that he is. Preferences are configuration under ADR-0031. Every place below is matched as whole words on the folded location text, never as a substring.
max_age_days_note: D14: 'i do not want a job post more than a week old', judged once, at first sight (his correction of 2026-09-26, ADR-0052): a posting first seen more than this many days after its publication date is dropped, and one admitted stays admitted however long it waits. A posting whose date is not proven to be a publication date (Lever's createdAt) is never dropped for age.
home_note: Places in Pakistan. A location naming one is eligible. Hyderabad is left out on purpose: India has one too, and 'Hyderabad, India' must not read as Pakistan.
home_country_codes_note: The home country's ISO 3166 alpha-2 code, as a source structures a posting's place: Lever's country. Where the location text names nothing the rule knows, a structured place decides, and only to close: a posting the source places in any other country is out, one it places here is kept, one it places nowhere keeps the text's verdict. The operator's go, 2026-10-02.
home_country_note: Which of the home places is the country rather than a city. 'Pakistan (On-site)' names no city, so it may be Karachi and is kept; an on-site posting is out only when it names a home city other than Karachi. A dropped posting's reason names these, so it says what was absent without any module naming a country.
onsite_home_city_note: D13: 'any onsite post besides karachi, pakistan are automatically out'. A Pakistan location that says it is on site or hybrid is eligible only in these cities. One that says neither is kept, since whether it is on site cannot be read from it.
remote_note: Remote with no place named is eligible. Beside a country it is that country's remote, as in 'Remote, Germany', and closed. Beside an on-site word it is a remote option, as in 'Remote/Hybrid - Lahore', and eligible.
open_note: Worldwide, and regions that can include Pakistan. A location naming one is eligible even beside a closed country, as in 'US, Canada, Asia', unless it says only, as in 'Global (US only)', or scopes it, as in 'anywhere in the US'. D13: 'if they say that they are hiring from anywhere like worldwide or lets say no mention of a country then they should be filtered in'.
closed_note: Countries other than Pakistan, their common short forms, and regions that cannot include it. A location every part of which names one of these, and no home place, is out: 'if there is an ai engineer post from usa and it says only us people then i am out'. A part naming nothing known is kept, so an unrecognised spelling can only let a posting through, never lose one.
stated_levels_dropped_note: The levels that drop a posting where a source states one, compared folded. A posting is dropped only when every level it states is one of these; one that states none, or states a value naming no level here, is kept. Until 2026-10-17 this was a list of the levels kept (Entry-level and Mid-level, the operator's option A of 2026-10-02, 'keep till mid'), which gave the same verdicts on Himalayas' six levels (Entry-level, Mid-level, Senior, Manager, Director, Executive) but dropped a value it did not name. His rule of 2026-10-10 for every source: every level from the start of a career up to mid is kept, whatever a source calls it, so Workable's Entry level, Associate and Mid-Senior level and SmartRecruiters' internship, entry and mid-senior levels are all kept, and only the levels above drop. His decision of 2026-10-16 (ADR-0032): Senior no longer drops by itself; it left this list on 2026-11-01, when the description's years decide (ADR-0058). The level is not the job type: interns, contract, part-time, temporary and volunteer roles are all kept, on every source, his decision of 2026-10-02.
header_place_sources_note: Sources whose place is free text in a post's first line, Hacker News' thread and job stories. The line's parts no place rule can name, its company, role and pay, are left out of the place, and with nothing left a post on site or hybrid with no remote option is closed: ADR-0057's row of 2026-10-18, the operator's '1. a.', an exception for these sources alone to keeping a place the rule cannot name. A part naming Pakistan is judged as before, Karachi kept and any other Pakistani city on site closed.
max_years_experience_note: The operator, 2026-10-02: 'the most it can say is 3+ and not 4+ years like 3 or 3+ is the max accepted years'. A posting whose description asks for more is out, required or preferred alike: 'the preferred should not count as required ... but then again ... 5+ years preferred is already out since the max is 3 or 3+ years'. A range counts by its low end, so '3 to 5 years' is kept, and a line that opens the role to fresh graduates is not read as a minimum. A description stating no figure keeps the posting. His reference maximum since 2026-09-17, when he deferred the rule until descriptions were read.
